id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

title:
A deployment package file is a zip file containing the files requirement by an application.
Following file types are accepted:
 - *.c3typ; *.c3app; *.c3ui: module definitions. Module definition files in the .zip must be in the sub folder
      with the same name as package where this module belongs.
 - *.js : the action implementations associated with the module definitions.
     The javascript files must be in a directory named after the module name.
 - *.json : the data that should be upserted as part of this deployment.
     There are two ways to package the json files:
        1. ${package}/${module}/${type}.json: a directory named after the module name contains a file named
            after the type name.
        2. ${package}/${module}/${type}/data1.json: if you have multiple data files for the same type,
            you can package them up in a directory named after the module name containing a directory named
             after the type name.
 - binary attachments: an 'attachments' directory might contains random binary files.
    These files might be used if you provide data for BundleAttachment type.


Example:
  +- attachments
  |  |- helloworld.ear
  |  +- dir1
  |     |- config.xml
  |
  +- package1
  |  +- foo
  |  |  |- fooFunction1.js
  |  |  |- fooFunction2.js
  |  |  |- fooType1.json
  |  +- bar
  |  |  |- barFunction1.js
  |  |  |- barFunction2.js
  |  |  +- barType1
  |  |     |- jsonData1.json
  |  |     |- jsonData2.json
  |  |- foo.c3typ
  |  |- foo.c3app
  |  |- bar.c3typ
  |
  +- package2
     |- baz.c3ui
